Class Effect

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.tfx.Effect
public final class Effect extends Object
Represents an effect that can be applied to terminal cells.

The Effect class is a wrapper around a Shader that provides a fluent, immutable API for configuring effects. It separates the effect implementation (Shader) from the effect configuration (Effect), allowing effects to be easily composed and customized without modifying the underlying shader.

Design Philosophy:

  • Immutability: All configuration methods return new Effect instances, making effects safe to share and compose.
  • Separation of Concerns: Effects handle configuration and lifecycle, while Shaders handle the actual rendering logic.
  • Fluent API: Method chaining allows for readable effect construction.

Usage Pattern: 

Effect fade = Fx.fadeToFg(Color.CYAN, 2000, Interpolation.SineInOut)
    .withFilter(CellFilter.text())
    .withColorSpace(TFxColorSpace.HSL)
    .withPattern(SweepPattern.leftToRight(10.0f));

Effects are stateful and should be processed each frame until they complete. Use EffectManager to manage multiple effects and their lifecycle.

    • setArea

      public void setArea(Rect area)
      Updates the area where this effect is applied.

      Unlike withArea(Rect) which creates a new Effect, this method mutates the existing effect. This is useful for updating running effects when elements move or resize.

      Parameters:
      area - The new area where the effect should be applied

    • process

      public TFxDuration process(TFxDuration duration, Buffer buffer, Rect area)
      Processes the effect for the given duration.

      This method: 1. Updates the shader's timer with the given duration 2. Executes the shader effect 3. Returns any overflow duration

      Parameters:
      duration - The duration to process the effect for
      buffer - The buffer where the effect will be applied
      area - The rectangular area within the buffer where the effect will be applied
      Returns:
      The overflow duration if the effect is done, or null if still running

    • copy

      public Effect copy()
      Creates a copy of this effect with a fresh internal state.

      The copy has the same configuration (area, filter, color space, pattern, loop mode) but its own independent timer state. This is useful when you need to apply the same effect to multiple elements independently.

      Returns:
      A new Effect instance that is a copy of this one

    • reversed

      public Effect reversed()
      Creates a new Effect with the shader's reverse flag toggled.

      This reverses the playback direction of the effect, causing it to play backwards.

      In Rust, this takes ownership and mutates in place, but in Java we create a new immutable instance to match the behavior of EffectTimer.reversed().

      Returns:
      A new Effect instance with the shader's reverse flag toggled

    • loop

      public Effect loop()
      Creates a new Effect that loops continuously from the beginning.

      When the effect reaches its end, it resets to the beginning and continues running. Looping effects never complete on their own and must be manually removed or cleared from the effect manager.

      Example: 

      Effect looping = Fx.fadeToFg(Color.CYAN, 1000, Interpolation.SineInOut)
    .loop();
      Returns:
      A new Effect instance with continuous looping enabled

    • pingPong

      public Effect pingPong()
      Creates a new Effect that ping-pongs back and forth.

      When the effect reaches its end, it reverses direction and plays backwards. When it reaches the beginning, it reverses again. This creates a smooth back-and-forth animation. Ping-pong effects never complete on their own and must be manually removed or cleared from the effect manager.

      Example: 

      Effect pingPong = Fx.fadeToFg(Color.CYAN, 1000, Interpolation.SineInOut)
    .pingPong();
      Returns:
      A new Effect instance with ping-pong looping enabled
